instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Script: Gurmukhi. Used in Punjab and Chandigarh, and spoken in Delhi and
Haryana.
Tone: everyday spoken Punjabi.
Words: ਆਨਲਾਈਨ, ਫਾਰਮ, ਪੋਰਟਲ, ਲੌਗਇਨ, ਆਧਾਰ, ਬੈਂਕ, ਮੋਬਾਈਲ, OTP, ਹੈਲਪਲਾਈਨ, ਸਰਟੀਫਿਕੇਟ,
ਡਾਊਨਲੋਡ, ਅਪਲੋਡ.
UI: ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਿਓ, ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰੋ, ਅੱਗੇ, ਪਿੱਛੇ, ਖੋਜੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਸੈਟਿੰਗਾਂ, ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਮਦਦ.
Offices: ਤਹਿਸੀਲਦਾਰ, ਪਟਵਾਰੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ, ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਪੰਚਾਇਤ, ਡਿਪਟੀ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨਰ.
Gender: ਲਿੰਗ. Money: ₹6,000; ₹8 ਲੱਖ. September: ਸਤੰਬਰ.

## Odia (or)

Script: Odia. Used in Odisha.
Tone: everyday spoken Odia.
Words: ଅନଲାଇନ, ଫର୍ମ, ପୋର୍ଟାଲ, ଲଗଇନ, ଆଧାର, ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ, ମୋବାଇଲ, OTP, ହେଲ୍ପଲାଇନ, ସାର୍ଟିଫିକେଟ,
ଡାଉନଲୋଡ, ଅପଲୋଡ.
UI: ଆବେଦନ କରନ୍ତୁ, ଦାଖଲ କରନ୍ତୁ, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ, ପଛକୁ, ଖୋଜନ୍ତୁ, ସେୟାର କରନ୍ତୁ, ସେଟିଂସ୍, ଭାଷା, ସାହାଯ୍ୟ.
Offices: ତହସିଲଦାର, ବିଡିଓ, ଗ୍ରାମ ପଞ୍ଚାୟତ, ଜିଲ୍ଲାପାଳ (କଲେକ୍ଟର), ମୋ ସେବା କେନ୍ଦ୍ର.

Death and disability help is for registered workers aged 18 to 60. Maternity help is for a registered woman worker who delivers in a government hospital, for up to two births

The 8-digit family number from the same Samagra slip. Your name, age and address are then filled in from Samagra.

Pick the work you actually do for a living. Gig workers, such as delivery riders, can choose platform work.

From the first page of your passbook. The account must be in your own name and Aadhaar-seeded.

Make sure your Samagra record is e-KYC'd with Aadhaar, on samagra.gov.in or at the gram panchayat or ward office.
Open sambal.mp.gov.in and choose Apply for registration (पंजीयन हेतु आवेदन करें). Enter your Samagra ID, family ID and the captcha. The panchayat or ward office can also do this for you.
Fill in the type of work, the nominee and the bank details, then submit. Note the application number and the name of the inquiry officer shown on screen.

The inquiry officer, usually the panchayat secretary or ward in-charge, checks your details. Then the Janpad Panchayat or municipal office approves the application. Track it under Application status (संबल आवेदन की स्थिति).
Once approved, download your Sambal card from the portal. If you are rejected, you can appeal online to the SDM (पंजीयन अपील).

For maternity help, register the pregnancy at the government hospital or with the ANM. Rs 4,000 comes after the checkups and Rs 12,000 after delivery in a government hospital, straight into your bank account.

On a death, the panchayat secretary or ward in-charge pays Rs 5,000 funeral help at once. The family applies at the Janpad or municipal office for the Rs 2 lakh or Rs 4 lakh, which is paid into the nominee's account.
State Health Agency (Deendayal Swasthya Suraksha Parishad), Public Health and Family Welfare Department, Madhya Pradesh

Madhya Pradesh runs Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY under the name Niramayam, and the state pays for many more families than the central list covers. Every family holding an NFSA food-grain slip (khadyann parchi) qualifies, as do Sambal and construction workers, ASHA and anganwadi workers, and everyone aged 70 or above. Each family gets free, cashless treatment up to Rs 5 lakh a year in empanelled government and private hospitals. You can make the card yourself on the Ayushman portal or app, or free at a Lok Seva Kendra, CSC or the hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk.
Rs 5 lakh a year per family, cashless, in empanelled hospitals
Families holding an NFSA food-grain eligibility slip (khadyann parchi) in Madhya Pradesh
Families in the SECC 2011 list (the central PM-JAY list)
Workers registered under Sambal or with the Building and Other Construction Workers Board, and their families
ASHA workers, anganwadi workers and helpers, PVTG families (Baiga, Bharia, Sahariya), Bhopal gas tragedy victims and Dharti Aaba (DAJGUA) beneficiaries
Every person aged 70 or above, whatever the income (Ayushman Vay Vandana card)
No limit on family size or age; illnesses you already have are covered from day one
Aadhaar card of each family member who needs a card
Samagra ID and the NFSA food-grain slip or ration card

Choose Beneficiary when making the card for yourself or your family.

You can also search by family, name or PMJAY ID. If nothing comes up, check at the ration shop that your name is on the NFSA slip.

Log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP, choose PMJAY and Madhya Pradesh, and search for your family by Aadhaar.
Pick the member marked eKYC pending, verify with Aadhaar OTP or face scan, take the live photo, and fill in the relation, district and PIN code. Submit.
The State Health Agency usually approves within a day or two. Log in again and download the card. It is also made free at a Lok Seva Kendra, CSC, government hospital or Aapke Dwar Niramayam camp.
At the hospital, go to the Ayushman Mitra desk with the card or Aadhaar. Treatment listed under the scheme is cashless up to Rs 5 lakh a year. Find empanelled hospitals at hem.nha.gov.in.
If any hospital asks you for money for a covered treatment, call 14555 or the CM Helpline 181.
14555 (Ayushman Bharat MP helpline), 1800-233-2085 (Ayushman Bharat), CM Helpline 181
Mukhyamantri Ladli Laxmi Yojana (Ladli Laxmi 2.0)
Department of Women and Child Development, Madhya Pradesh

When a girl is born in Madhya Pradesh and registered under this scheme, the state issues a certificate in her name promising Rs 1,43,000 in stages. She gets scholarships when she joins classes 6, 9, 11 and 12, Rs 25,000 when she joins college, and Rs 1 lakh at age 21. The state also pays her college tuition fees. Parents should apply within one year of her birth, either online themselves or through the anganwadi.
Rs 1,43,000 in stages: Rs 18,000 school scholarships, Rs 25,000 for college, Rs 1 lakh at 21
Girl born on or after 1 January 2006 and registered at the local anganwadi centre
Parents are original residents of Madhya Pradesh and do not pay income tax
Parents have two children or fewer. The first girl qualifies without any condition. For the second girl, the mother or father must have adopted family planning after the second child
Apply within one year of the girl's birth. Late cases, orphans, adopted girls and girls who have lost a parent can be registered up to age 5 as special cases
The final Rs 1 lakh is paid only if she has appeared for the class 12 exam and was not married before 18
Samagra family ID, with the girl added as a member and her 9-digit Samagra member ID
Photo of the girl with her mother or father (JPG or PNG, 40 to 200 KB)
Family planning (sterilisation) certificate, if this is the second girl

After class 12, when she joins a college or professional course of at least two years, apply under the graduation incentive link (प्रोत्साहन राशि) with her Ladli registration number for Rs 25,000, paid in two halves in the first and last year. At 21 she gets Rs 1 lakh.
Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY / Ayushman Card)
Public Health Department, Government of Maharashtra (State Health Assurance Society)

Free, cashless hospital treatment for every family in Maharashtra, up to Rs.5 lakh a family each year, at government and private hospitals that have joined the scheme. Since 1 July 2024 it runs together with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, so one Ayushman card works for both, and families with a white ration card, or with no ration card but a Maharashtra domicile certificate, are covered as well. It was earlier called Rajiv Gandhi Jeevandayee Arogya Yojana. There is nothing to apply for in advance: at the hospital, the Arogyamitra desk registers the patient with the ration card and Aadhaar.
Rs.5 lakh a year per family, cashless, at network hospitals
Every family living in Maharashtra, whatever its income (universal cover since 1 July 2024)
Families with a yellow, Antyodaya (AAY), Annapurna, orange or white ration card
A family with no ration card is covered if it holds a Maharashtra domicile certificate
The Rs.5 lakh is shared by the whole family in a year (family floater), and illnesses you already have are covered from the first day
Covers listed surgeries and hospital treatments in 34 specialities at network hospitals in Maharashtra; in 2025 the state approved widening the list from 1,356 to 2,399 procedures
Ration card of any colour (yellow, orange, white, AAY or Annapurna)
Maharashtra domicile certificate, if the family has no ration card
Mobile number for the OTP during Aadhaar e-KYC
Ayushman card, if already made (it is not needed to start treatment)

The Arogyamitra desk at any MJPJAY network (empanelled) hospital in Maharashtra, government or private; it is usually near the main reception. Take the original ration card (or the domicile certificate) and the patient's Aadhaar card. The list of network hospitals is on jeevandayee.gov.in and is also given on the toll-free number 155388. The Ayushman card itself can be made beforehand at a CSC (Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra), through the ASHA worker, or at the same hospital desk.
The 12-digit number printed on the ration card. The Arogyamitra uses it to find your whole family in the scheme list.
Yellow, orange, white, AAY or Annapurna are all accepted. If you have no ration card, show the Maharashtra domicile certificate instead.
Exactly as printed on the patient's Aadhaar card, so that the e-KYC matches.
The patient's own Aadhaar, not the head of family's. An OTP, fingerprint or face scan confirms it.
How the patient is related to the person named first on the ration card.
A number someone in the family keeps with them; messages about approval and discharge come here.
The doctor writes this after examining the patient. The hospital then asks the scheme for approval of that package.
In an emergency the hospital starts treatment at once and informs the scheme by phone or email; the papers can follow.

When a doctor says the patient needs an operation or admission, ask whether the hospital is an MJPJAY / Ayushman network hospital. If you are not sure, call 155388 or look up the hospital list on jeevandayee.gov.in.
Go to the Arogyamitra desk with the ration card and the patient's Aadhaar. The Arogyamitra registers the patient on the scheme portal and does the Aadhaar e-KYC by OTP, fingerprint or face scan.

The doctor examines the patient, and the hospital sends a pre-authorisation request online to the State Health Assurance Society with the reports. Approval usually comes within hours; in an emergency, treatment starts first.
Once approved, the listed treatment, operation, medicines, tests, bed and food are free. Do not pay cash or sign any paper promising to pay for a listed treatment.
At discharge you receive the discharge summary. The hospital's bill goes to the government, not to you.
If a hospital asks for money for a covered treatment, call 155388 or 1800-233-2200 before paying and tell them the hospital's name.
To make the next visit quicker, get the Ayushman card made for every family member at a CSC, through the ASHA worker or at the Arogyamitra desk.
155388 / 1800-233-2200 (MJPJAY toll-free call centre); 14555 (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY)
Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana (Niradhar Pension)
Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Government of Maharashtra (through the Tehsildar)

A monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for people under 65 who have no one to support them: persons with 40% or more disability, people with serious illnesses such as cancer, TB, HIV or leprosy, widows, divorced or abandoned women, orphan children and transgender persons, among others. Disabled beneficiaries get Rs.2,500 a month from October 2025. The money comes every month by DBT into an Aadhaar-linked bank account. You apply through the talathi or the tehsil office; the state has also opened online applications on the MahaDBT portal.
Rs.1,500 a month (Rs.2,500 for disabled beneficiaries)
Living in Maharashtra for at least 15 years; aged 18 to below 65 (orphan or disabled children under 18 get it through a guardian)
Family income up to Rs.21,000 a year, or up to Rs.50,000 a year if the applicant is disabled; or the family is on the BPL list

Belongs to a destitute group: disabled (40% or more, UDID card needed), serious illness, widow, divorced or abandoned woman, woman whose divorce is pending, unmarried woman of 35 or more with no support, orphan child, transgender person, or the family of a farmer who died by suicide
